div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 161px; margin-left: 1389px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
When you see a weight field in a Kubernetes YAML file,
you are essentially "tuning" the Scoring Phase (not the Filtering phase)
from the outside.
You are telling the scheduler how much importance it should
give to that specific rule compared to its default internal rules.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 250px; margin-left: 1389px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
The scheduler takes the weight you defined (1 to 100)
and adds it to the scores for any node that satisfies that condition.
For example:
Weight 100: You are saying, "I REALLY want this. This rule should probably
override almost every other default scoring function (like ImageLocality or LeastAllocated)."
Weight 1: You are saying, "This would be nice, but if the node is a bit busy or doesn't have the image, don't worry about it."

g.text: You will notice there is no weight field for requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.
Why? Because "Required" is a filter, not a score
